description:
The E5-B resampler's lerp (a + (b - a) * frac) is exactly the f32 op
sequence filmcraft's StreamResampler rounds (three roundings: sub,
mul, add). The default fp-contract collapses it into one fmadd — one
rounding where the crate has three — so the crate-vector tests would
pin the wrong numbers and the one-sample-lag output would round
differently on desktop vs phone vs any later JNI wiring.

Measured proof (this is why (b) symmetric-safety, not (a) "lerp is
safe"): compiling core/src/Resample.cpp for arm64 both ways —
Apple clang 21 host arm64 and the NDK r57 clang 21
(aarch64-linux-android34, the phone's actual compiler) — the default
emits 2 fmadd in process(), the opt-out emits 0. The tolerance-based
tone tests would pass either way today; what breaks is the "the
numbers filmcraft runs" contract (tests) and the cross-target
identity the E5-B wiring package will need against AudioMixe
